Après avoir grandi à Pointe-Noire et Bra: After growing up in Pointe-Noire and Brazzaville, Meddy Makanga left his native Congo at 14 to settle in Montréal, where his parents had already been living for four years. His father, Médard Makanga, a former sprinter who took part in the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, moved there at the end of his professional career to be able to offer his family more opportunities.
« Il a beaucoup voyagé dans le monde, ma: “He travelled a lot around the world, but when he got to Canada, he really liked the country and decided to settle here,” Meddexx sums up. Adjusting, however, was not easy for the teenager he was then.
« En Afrique, on a une façon de vivre et: “In Africa, we have a different way of living and acting. You greet strangers there. The people in the neighbourhood are family. Back home, you can hold your guy friend’s hand, walk together, and nothing happens. But you get here, and people react,” he offers as an example.
Le système d’éducation était également b: The education system was also very different, which at first left him feeling somewhat insecure. “Over time, by accomplishing things, one little thing after another, I gained confidence. But it was a very hard start,” he reveals.
« Je crois que la coiffure a fait un peu: “I think hairstyling made me a bit of the person I am today. I was shy and withdrawn, but through cutting hair, I learned to express myself. The funny side I have, I was able to develop it in a barbershop,” Mr. Makanga confides.
Selon lui, c’est sa décision de commence: According to him, what changed the game was his decision to start posting videos on YouTube, then on Instagram, and sharing his work there, which brought him good feedback and more confidence.
« Au début, c’était très niché, mais ave: “In the beginning, it was very niche, but over time I ended up getting better. You become creative by creating. When you create, it’s often accidental. Something happens and gives an unexpected result,” he says.
Un client travaillant dans l’événementie: A client who worked in the events industry put him in touch with Franco-Congolese singer Gims. Since then, he has also had the chance to cut the hair of NLE Choppa, Dadju, Tayc, Josh Segarra and Georges St-Pierre, among other celebrities.
« Je suis reconnaissant. Je n’ai pas la: “I’m grateful. I don’t have a big head. It’s true that it can touch your ego, but I try to keep my feet on the ground.
